{{nihongo|'''Otsuki Shrine'''|小槻神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

=== Enshrined God ===
The following two deities are enshrined.
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ochibetsu no Mikoto}} (Ochiwake no Mikoto)
*: Also written as ``Rakubetsu no Mikoto'' or ``Sobetsu no Mikoto.'' He was the 11th {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}{{ill|Imperial Prince|ja|皇子|ko|황자|vi|Hoàng tử|zh|皇子|zh_min_nan|Hông-chú|qid=Q12886381}} and the ancestor of {{ill|Kotsukiyama-kun|Q11462129|qid=Q11462129}} ({{ill|Ozuki clan|Q11462133|qid=Q11462133}}). Depending on the literature, the notation ``{{ill|Prince Ikobayawake no Mikoto|Q11492324|qid=Q11492324}}'' is also seen, but Issokubetsu no Mikoto is a half-brother of Ochibetsu no Mikoto.
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amagoyane Mikoto}} (Amenokoyane Mikoto)

=== History ===
{{ill|Ancient history|Q41493|qid=Q41493}} in {{ill|Kurita District, Shiga|Q6446084|qid=Q6446084}} (current {{ill|Kusatsu, Shiga|Q386677|qid=Q386677}}, {{jalink|Ritto City|Q It is said that the shrine was founded by {{ill|Otsukiyama-kun|Q11462129|qid=Q11462129}} (Kozukiyama-kō), a powerful family from the 857310}} area, who enshrined {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ochibetsu-no-Mikoto}} as the ancestral deity. Since Otsukiyama-kun presented {{ill|Imperial Court of Japan|Q30253177|qid=Q30253177|lt=Imperial Court}} with {{ill|Uneme|Q11644506|qid=Q11644506}}, it is assumed that he belonged to a family in the Kurita County {{ill|Gunji|Q4152149|qid=Q4152149}} class. Otsukiyama-kun is {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan}} in {{ill|Heian-kyō|Q751907|qid=Q751907|lt=Kyoto}} in 15 years ({{ill|873|Q30369|qid=Q30369}}) He later moved to the {{ill|Ozuki clan|Q11462133|qid=Q11462133}} ({{ill|official|Q11452088|qid=Q11452088}} family) and became a member of the {{jalink|Imperial court}. === Precincts ===
The precincts adjoin the ruins of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aochi Castle}} from the Sengoku period. The main shrine is a three-room shrine {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684}}{{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}}, with a frontage of three rooms and a depth of two rooms. It was constructed in 1896. The worship hall is {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}}, and has a frontage of three rooms and a depth of three rooms.

It is also said that there were a group of ancient tombs within the precincts, and stone walls were built using the stones excavated from the tombs. In addition, the tree that is 18 meters tall and estimated to be over 100 years old is designated as a famous tree of Kusatsu City.

=== Cultural assets ===

=== Cultural property designated by Kusatsu City ===
*Tangible cultural property
** Wooden seated statue of the male god (sculpture) - Made in the late Heian period. {{ill|Ionoi Shrine|Q22117831|qid=Q22117831}}It has been pointed out that it resembles a statue of a male deity. Designated on July 27, 2017 (Heisei 29) <ref>{{PDFlink|[https://www.city.kusatsu.shiga.jp/shisei/shichoshitsu/kaikentaiwa/kishakaikei/h29/20170727.files/2-1.pdf Regarding the new designation as a tangible cultural property designated by Kusatsu City]}} (Kusatsu City homepage). </ref><ref>[https://mainichi.jp/articles/20170829/ddl/k25/040/564000c "Three new municipal tangible cultural properties designated: late Heian period, wooden male god seated statues, Kusatsu Shiga"]{{broken link|date=July 2023}} (Mainichi Shimbun, August 29, 2017). </ref>.

* '''Transportation'''
** {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125|lt=JR}}{{ill|Biwako Line|Q804135|qid=Q804135}} ({{ill|Tōkaidō Main Line|Q1190152|qid=Q1190152}})/JR Kusatsu Line{{jalink|Kusatsu Station (Shiga Prefecture)|Q775813|About 15 minutes by car or 50 minutes on foot from Kusatsu Station.
** From the same station, take the bus ({{ill|Teisan Konan Transport|Q11481075|qid=Q11481075}}) and get off at the "Shizu Elementary School" stop, then walk for 5 minutes (*Shinmei Shrine is a 2-minute walk).
